editorNote: Christmas week finds the personal computer moving from hobby counter to mainstream symbol, with TIME preparing to crown the computer as its Machine of the Year while shoppers compare Atari, Commodore, TI, and IBM-compatible possibilities.
morningLine: On newsstands and shop counters this week: the home computer becomes a holiday conversation piece, Tootsie leads the movie weekend, and Maneater keeps its hold on pop radio.

lead.headline: The Computer Moves In for Christmas Week
lead.summary: TIME's Jan. 3, 1983 cover package names the computer its Machine of the Year, matching what holiday shoppers can see in stores: personal machines are being sold as family, school, office, and game-room tools rather than as curiosities for specialists.

market.headline: The microcomputer becomes mainstream shorthand
market.summary: By the end of 1982, the industry story is no longer just which machine is fastest. The cultural shift is that magazines, schools, offices, and department stores are all treating computers as ordinary household decisions.
